costNote: Making the products, before amortization. Abbott reports the $841M of intangible amortization as its own line (in running costs below, in this chart) because it mostly comes from acquisitions — it doubled with the Exact Sciences deal.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Up 40% as Abbott absorbs Exact Sciences (closed March 2026) and carries legal-settlement and deal-related charges inside specified items.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Up 20% — the pipeline absorbed Exact Sciences' cancer-diagnostics research on top of Abbott's own programs.

opex.name: Amortization of intangibles
opex.note: Writing down the value of technology and brands bought in past deals. Doubled year over year after Exact Sciences.

otherDetail.label: Interest expense, net
otherDetail.note: Interest on a bigger debt pile after acquisition financing, net of interest earned. Was just $44M a year ago.

otherDetail.label: Other income & FX, net
otherDetail.note: $164M of other income plus a $6M currency gain.

oneTimers.label: Specified items — $1.56B after tax
oneTimers.text: GAAP results exclude nothing; adjusted EPS of $1.42 strips out $1.557B of after-tax charges ($0.89/share): intangible amortization, legal settlements, Exact Sciences acquisition and restructuring costs.

segments.name: Medical Devices
segments.note: The biggest business — glucose sensors (Libre), heart devices, electrophysiology. Up 6.9% reported, 7.8% comparable; Libre Duo (glucose + ketone) won FDA approval in August.

segments.name: Diagnostics
segments.note: Reported sales jumped 46.7% because Exact Sciences (cancer screening, incl. Cologuard) joined in March; underlying comparable growth was 6.4%.

segments.name: Nutrition
segments.note: Similac and adult nutrition (Ensure). Up 5.1%, led by pediatric nutrition at nearly +9%.

segments.name: Established Pharmaceuticals
segments.note: Branded generics sold outside the US. Sold entirely internationally.

sources.label: Abbott Q3 2026 earnings release — SEC EDGAR Ex-99.1 (8-K, Oct 21, 2026)

takeaways.text: GAAP EPS fell 44% to $0.53 as specified items hit $1.56B after tax — amortization, legal settlements and Exact Sciences deal costs. The adjusted number Abbott steers by was $1.42, up modestly.
takeaways.title: GAAP profit halved by deal charges

takeaways.text: Reported sales rose 14.5% with Exact Sciences included; on the comparable basis Abbott prefers (both years incl. Exact) growth was 7.0% — balanced across all four divisions.
takeaways.title: Underlying growth is 7%

takeaways.text: Abbott tightened full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $5.50–$5.55 and expects Q4 adjusted EPS of $1.62–$1.67, with comparable sales growth of about 6% for the year.
takeaways.title: Guidance tightened, not cut

verdict: Growth is real but expensive: sales up 14.5% with Exact Sciences aboard, while deal costs halved GAAP profit.
